channel.title: Volvo recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Volvo VNL and VNR trucks may lose roof marker lights
item.description: Volvo Trucks North America is recalling certain 2026-2027 VNL (4) and VNR (4) trucks. The center marker lights on the roof of the cab may fail to light up. Because of that, these trucks do not meet the federal rule for lamps, reflectors and related equipment. Dealers will replace the center roof marker light free of charge. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 5, 2026, and the affected VINs will be searchable on NHTSA.gov starting August 13, 2026.

item.title: Volvo Truck Steering Arm May Loosen, Crash Risk
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain trucks because the steering knuckles may have been built with the steering arms not tightened enough. A loose steering arm can affect the vehicle's steering, since the connection between the steering arm and the steering knuckle isn't as secure as it should be. This loss of a secure connection can make it harder for the driver to steer the truck as intended.

item.title: Volvo Trucks Wheel Lug Nuts May Loosen
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VAH, VN, VHD, VNL, and VNR vehicles because the wheel lug nuts may loosen and allow a wheel to detach.

item.title: Volvo Trucks Rear Brake Modulator Short Circuit Risk
item.description: On some VNR and VNL trucks, the electrical connectors on the rear brake modulators are not protected. These connectors can short circuit, and if that happens, the truck can lose its anti-lock braking system and electronic stability control.

item.title: Volvo VNL Turn Signals May Malfunction
item.description: Volvo is recalling certain VNL and VNR trucks because the turn signals may not work properly. A turn signal that doesn't work as it should cannot reliably show other drivers which direction the truck is about to turn. Because of this, the affected trucks do not meet a federal safety standard covering lights, reflective devices, and other equipment used to signal a driver's intentions on the road. The recall covers software used to control the turn signal indicators.

item.title: Volvo VNL Trucks Brakes May Release Slowly
item.description: The service brakes on these trucks may take longer than expected to release after the brake pedal is applied. This means that when the driver lets off the brake, the brakes may stay engaged longer than they should. A delayed brake release can increase the risk of a crash. To fix this, dealers will install an additional brake valve and fittings into the brake system's air lines, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Volvo VNL Trucks Instrument Panel May Fail While Driving
item.description: The instrument panel in these trucks may fail while the vehicle is being driven. When this happens, the driver may not be able to see important safety information, such as the speedometer or warning lights. Not being able to see this information while driving increases the risk of a crash. To fix this, dealers will replace the instrument panel cluster, and this repair will be done at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Volvo EX30 seat belt chime may not sound
item.description: The seat belt warning system in these vehicles may fail to play the audible chime that is supposed to alert an unbelted occupant. This means the vehicle doesn't fully meet a federal safety standard for occupant protection.

item.title: Volvo EX30 Battery May Overheat and Catch Fire
item.description: On certain EX30 vehicles, the high voltage battery may short circuit and overheat. Until the repair is complete, owners are advised to limit charging to a maximum of 70%. Dealers will inspect the battery and replace battery modules as necessary, free of charge.

item.title: Volvo VNL trucks may lack enough parking brake force
item.description: Some 2024-2027 Volvo VNL trucks without auxiliary parking brakes may not have enough weight on the parking brake axle when the truck is in weight bias mode. This can result in the parking brake not applying enough force. Dealers will replace the brake chambers, free of charge.

item.title: Volvo EX30 High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk
item.description: Some Volvo EX30 vehicles have a high-voltage battery that may experience a short circuit. When this happens, the battery can overheat.

item.title: Volvo rearview camera image may not appear in reverse
item.description: Volvo is recalling a range of recent Volvo cars and SUVs. When the driver shifts into reverse, the picture from the rearview camera may not come up on the screen. Because of that, these vehicles do not meet the federal rear visibility safety rule. A dealer can install updated software, or the update can be sent to the car over the air. This recall replaces an earlier Volvo recall, and cars already repaired under that earlier recall need the new repair too.

item.title: Volvo Trucks Automatic High Beams May Stay On
item.description: On certain VNR and VNL trucks, the automatic high beam feature may fail to switch the headlights down to low beam when it should. As an interim fix, Volvo will send an over-the-air software update to turn off the automatic high beam feature.

item.title: Volvo VNL Trucks May Lose Secured Cargo Bars
item.description: On certain VNL trucks, the clamps that hold the load lock bars in place on the back of the cab may loosen over time. If a clamp loosens, the load lock bar it holds can come unsecured. Dealers will replace the load lock clamps.

item.title: Volvo VN trucks roof marker lights may not illuminate
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain new VN trucks because the marker lights in the center of the roof may not light up. These lights are meant to make the truck easier for other drivers to see. Since they may fail to come on, these trucks do not meet the federal safety rule for lamps, reflective devices and related equipment. A dealer will replace the center roof marker light at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Volvo VAH trucks may have weak seat belt anchor
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VAH trucks because the anchor that holds the passenger seat belt to the floor may fail. The floor underneath it was not reinforced enough to hold the anchor in place. Because of this, these trucks do not meet the federal safety rule for seat belt anchorages. If the anchor gives way, the seat belt cannot hold the person in the seat the way it is meant to.

item.title: Volvo EX90 Power Tailgate May Suddenly Drop
item.description: On certain 2025 Volvo EX90 vehicles, a nut that holds part of the power tailgate mechanism in place — called a spindle nut — may come loose and detach from the tailgate's drive units. If this happens, the power tailgate could suddenly drop instead of staying open or closing normally. A tailgate that drops unexpectedly could hit someone standing near it, which increases the risk of injury.

item.title: Volvo Trucks Door May Not Open From Inside
item.description: On some new Volvo VNL trucks, the cable that connects the interior door handle to the door latch may have been installed incorrectly. If this happens, the door may not open when someone tries to use the inside handle. This could trap a person inside the truck, which increases the risk of injury.

item.title: Volvo VNL trucks: trailer lights may not work
item.description: Some 2025-2026 Volvo VNL trucks have a body control module for the trailer lighting system that was not manufactured correctly. Because of this manufacturing problem, when the truck is towing a trailer, the trailer's tail lights and turn signals may fail to come on the way they are supposed to, even when the driver activates them.

item.title: Volvo VNL Truck Steering Assist Malfunction Risk
item.description: Some Volvo VNL trucks have a driver-assist feature that helps guide the truck's steering if it starts to oversteer. This feature may malfunction, and if it does, it can cause the driver to lose control of the truck's steering while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Volvo EX40, XC40, XC90 May Lose Brake Function
item.description: On some Volvo EX40, XC40, XC40 BEV, and XC90 PHEV vehicles, using "B" mode or One Pedal Drive while coasting down a hill in certain driving situations can cause the vehicle to lose brake function. Losing the ability to brake properly in this way can make it harder to slow down or stop the vehicle when needed, which increases the risk of a crash on the road.

item.title: Volvo rearview camera image may not appear in reverse
item.description: On these Volvo vehicles, the backup camera picture may not show up on the screen when you shift into reverse. The camera view is supposed to appear every time the vehicle is put in reverse, and because it may not, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for rear visibility. Volvo will fix this with a software update, either at a dealer or sent to the vehicle over the air.

item.title: Volvo VN and VNL Trucks Idler Gear Detaches
item.description: Volvo Trucks North America is recalling certain Volvo VN and VNL trucks because the fasteners on the idler gear bracket may not have been tightened properly. This can allow the idler gear to come loose from the engine.

item.title: Volvo VNL Trucks: Delayed Air Brake Response
item.description: Volvo is recalling certain New VN trucks because the air brakes may take longer than expected to start working once the driver presses the brake pedal. This means there could be a delay before the brakes fully engage when the driver tries to slow down or stop. Because of this delay in brake activation, the affected trucks do not meet a federal safety standard covering air brake systems on trucks like these.

item.title: Volvo EX90 Headlight Shutters May Close While Driving
item.description: Volvo is recalling certain EX90 vehicles because of a software error in the low power controller. This error can cause the headlight shutters to close over both the high and low beams while the vehicle is being driven. When the shutters close, the headlights stop putting out light, which can leave the driver with little or no forward lighting on the road.

item.title: Volvo EX90 Second-Row Seat Bolts May Be Loose
item.description: Volvo is recalling certain EX90 vehicles because the bolts for the second-row free-standing seat may not be tightened properly. A seat that isn't securely bolted down may not properly hold the occupant in place during a crash, which could increase the risk of injury. Dealers will inspect the seat bolts and tighten them as needed to correct the problem.

item.title: Volvo trucks' electronic control unit may misread signals
item.description: These trucks use a Bendix electronic control unit that can be affected by electrical noise and a low signal in the power line carrier. This can cause the unit to process commands incorrectly or to stop working. This affects certain Volvo VN, VAH, VHD, and VNRE trucks. Volvo Trucks is recalling these vehicles so dealers can reprogram the control unit's software.

item.title: Volvo Hybrid Models Brake Pedal Connection May Loosen
item.description: Certain Volvo S60, V60, S90, XC60 and XC90 hybrid vehicles may have a loose connection where the brake pedal links to the hydraulic brake unit, at a part called the pushrod screw joint. If this connection loosens, pressing the brake pedal may not properly engage the brakes. Dealers will inspect and tighten this connection as needed to fix the problem, free of charge.

item.title: Volvo VN Trucks Risk Unintended Acceleration
item.description: On certain 2022-2024 Volvo VN trucks, if communication on the vehicle's internal computer network is interrupted while the truck is in limp mode, the accelerator pedal signal can be read incorrectly. This can cause the truck to accelerate on its own.

item.title: Volvo XC40 left rear turn signal may not work
item.description: Volvo is recalling certain 2024 XC40 vehicles. A fault in the software that runs the car's central electronics module can stop the left rear turn signal from lighting up. The signal light on that corner of the car may simply not come on when the driver signals a turn. Volvo says the software can be updated by a dealer, or sent to the car as an over the air update, free of charge.

item.title: Volvo VN and VHD trucks carry wrong weight label
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VN and VHD trucks that have size 295/75 or 385/65 Continental tires on the front axle. The certification label on these trucks lists the wrong gross axle weight rating, the weight the axle is rated to carry. Because the listed rating is wrong, the truck can be loaded beyond what it should carry, and the truck does not meet the federal certification rule. Dealers will remove the label and put on a correct one, free of charge.

item.title: Volvo VN Truck Accelerator Sensor Disconnection Risk
item.description: Volvo is recalling certain VN trucks because the engine's throttle system may not return to idle fast enough if the sensor that reads the accelerator pedal position becomes disconnected. In plain terms, if that sensor comes loose, the engine could keep pushing power even after the driver lets off the gas pedal, instead of slowing back down right away as it's supposed to.

item.title: Volvo Truck Passenger Seat May Not Be Secured
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VN and VHD trucks because the passenger side bench seat may not be securely attached to the truck's floor. The attachment points holding the seat down may not be strong enough to keep it in place. To fix this, dealers will replace the weld nut with two nuts and a washer, strengthening how the seat is held to the floor. This repair will be done free of charge.

item.title: Volvo Truck Windshield Wiper Motor May Fail
item.description: On these trucks, the gears inside the windshield wiper motor may wear out sooner than they should, which can eventually cause the wiper motor to fail. When the wipers stop working, the driver has reduced visibility through the windshield. To correct this, dealers will replace the entire windshield wiper motor assembly on the affected trucks, at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Volvo VN, VAH Trucks Steering Fasteners May Loosen
item.description: On certain Volvo VN and VAH trucks, the fasteners that hold the steering gear in place may not have been tightened properly at the factory. Because these steering gear fasteners may be loose, they could work themselves looser over time as the truck is used.

item.title: Volvo VNL Trucks: Side Airbag May Not Deploy
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VNL and VHD trucks that are equipped with RollTek driver seats. On these trucks, a circuit needed for the side airbag is missing. Without this circuit in place, the side airbag will not deploy the way it is supposed to if the truck is involved in a crash. This means the airbag will not provide protection when needed.

item.title: Volvo VNR Electric Battery Coolant Line May Leak
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VNR Electric trucks. These trucks have a coolant line inside the high-voltage battery pack, and on affected trucks this coolant line may not be fully seated and locked into place. If the coolant line is not properly secured, coolant can leak out of the battery pack. A loss of coolant in this system can lead to an electrical short circuit inside the battery.

item.title: Volvo VNR Electric Adaptive Cruise Can Brake Hard
item.description: These electric trucks have adaptive cruise control that can apply the brakes on its own. Under light loads, that automatic braking can be much more aggressive than it should be. Braking that hard and suddenly can cause the rear wheels to skid, the brakes to lock up, or the driver to lose control of the truck. Losing control while braking raises the chance of a crash.

item.title: Volvo Steering Gear Screw May Lock Steering Wheel
item.description: On certain Volvo V60CC, XC60, and XC90 vehicles, the steering gear may have been assembled with two screws stacked on top of each other instead of one in the correct spot. One of these screws could come loose and fall inside the steering gearbox housing. If a screw ends up inside the gearbox, it can cause the steering wheel to lock up while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Volvo VNL Air Tank Bracket Fasteners May Break
item.description: The bolts that hold the air tank bracket in place on these trucks were tightened too much, and some may have broken. If a fastener breaks, the air tank can come loose from the truck. A tank that detaches while the truck is on the road becomes a hazard for other vehicles nearby, and it raises the chance of a crash.
